Architecture

PagePurpose
Failure and recovery playbookA visible error is preferable to a silent partial economic commit.
Multiplayer ownership and framework rolesPersistent facts have one durability owner and a current authority session; replication is a projection, not storage.
Persistence, schema and migrationsPostgreSQL stores records; UE Actors hold short-lived session projections.
Zone/server/backend topologyOne zone simulation per early dedicated process; one authenticated backend and one relational database.
Source-to-target migrationThe old offline platformer is historical evidence for documentation rigor, not the new MMO specification.
Transactions, receipts and concurrencyA reliable reward is an idempotent durable effect, not a claim that networks deliver a message exactly once.
Cross-zone handoff: one character, one writerIndividual ClientTravel connects a client to another dedicated server. It does not move the whole source population.

3D environment sourcing and productionThe character archive is not a 3D environment pack.
Animation compatibility and missing-art matrixAction support must be proven for each body/page/layer/facing combination.

Equipment slots are not sprite layersA valid item may provide stats even when its specific overlay is unavailable.
Private art import and PaperZD integrationImport only audited privately licensed source assets; all exact source frame coordinates remain blocked in this edition.
Sprite naming and sheet referenceA schema and audit workflow, not an invented frame atlas.

PagePurpose

DA_Class_ArcanistOffensive magic using common body.

Asset · Combat

PagePurpose
ARPGProjectileServer-simulated projectile actor with one hit-resolution owner and cosmetic remote movement.
BP_Projectile_ArcSparkEditor-tuned child of ARPGProjectile. Arcanist projectile definition; cosmetic fallback until art authored
BP_Projectile_TrainingArrowEditor-tuned child of ARPGProjectile. Ranger projectile definition; one server collision owner
URPGAbilitySystemComponentUse one Gameplay Ability System stack for health, mana, stamina, abilities, costs, cooldowns and effects. A player's ASC lives on PlayerState during one zone session; the current body is its avatar. An ordinary enemy owns its ASC on its Character.
URPGAttributeSetGAS attribute storage and change notification for Health/Mana/Stamina and derived combat values. Do not maintain parallel Character health variables.
URPGHitResolverSpatial attacks use real 3D collision queries while sprites communicate their timing. The server owns the active window, projectile spawn and effect application, and records which targets have already been attempted for each execution.
URPGTargetingComponentSoft targeting helps select an enemy or ally, but a selection does not guarantee a hit. Melee/projectile/area rules still use the server's current positions, collision, faction and ability definition.

Asset · Economy

PagePurpose

PagePurpose

URPGAdmissionValidatorTreat every network request as untrusted input. Authenticate identity at admission, validate ownership at every command and fence stale server sessions before they can write durable state. Security is a continuing process, not a claim that a dedicated server prevents cheating.
URPGReplicationPolicySend each client only relevant state while preserving gameplay correctness. Begin with generic Actor replication, then measure before choosing Iris or Replication Graph; do not enable both.
URPGTelemetryAdapterMake failures explainable without turning logging into another mutable gameplay database. Economic ledgers provide durable accounting; operational metrics explain latency, rejection and content balance.
URPGZoneHeartbeatComponentOperate a small persistent multi-zone game with measured capacities, reproducible builds, backups and a safe maintenance procedure. A dedicated UE process is a zone simulator, not a complete hosting or matchmaking platform.

TEST_Phase00Pin engine/toolchain/plugin evidence; establish paths, IDs, documentation and dedicated-server build prerequisites.
TEST_Phase01Prove a common body on 3D ground with four facings, zoom, depth, feet and a clothing fallback.
TEST_Phase02Use CharacterMovement across X/Y with Z height; add jump, sprint, dodge, swim and fall/shoreline rules.
TEST_Phase03Connect independent clients, possess once, replicate movement and remote appearance intent.
TEST_Phase04Use a development authenticator boundary; create/list/select a named class/body/appearance record.
TEST_Phase05Create the versioned schema, command receipts, session fencing and minimal reward/item identities.

TEST_Phase08Build server AI and defeat ledger, minimal party eligibility, XP awards and safe respawn.
TEST_Phase09Create real inventory UI/stack rules, item requirements and replicated logical/visual equipment.
TEST_Phase10Materialize loot once for a defeated spawn generation; expose corpse/container interaction.
TEST_Phase11Commit buy/sell/buyback/repair and deposits/withdrawals through authenticated service commands.
TEST_Phase12Select eligible sites per zone seed; validate tools, action leases, yield, XP and respawn.
TEST_Phase13Learn recipes, use stations and consume materials/currency atomically for deterministic items.
TEST_Phase14Validate shoreline casts, world bobber, bite window, reel and terminal fish reward.
TEST_Phase15Author conditional NPC dialogue and a quest DAG using server gameplay events and receipt-backed rewards.
TEST_Phase16Build all four ability catalogs, validated skill graph, derived stats and paid respec.
TEST_Phase17Add discovery/minimap, time/weather, six region plans and a data-driven content factory.
TEST_Phase18Add phases/telegraphs, four-player instanced ruin allocation and recovery/loot rules.
TEST_Phase19Extend minimal parties into invites/chat/friends/block/private messages and escrow trades.
TEST_Phase20Add faction thresholds, profession/class training, safe-hub unlocks and world event participation.
TEST_Phase21Add guild roles/invites, social dashboards, content expansion; mounts stay behind an art/movement gate.
TEST_Phase22Exercise restarts, restores, fencing, dupe attacks, deployment and replication comparisons.
TEST_Phase23Run complete packaged client/server slices, localization/accessibility and documentation consistency.
URPGAcceptanceHarnessProve the integrated player journey in a real packaged client/server environment, while distinguishing documentation static checks from gameplay verification. Release only the measured, tested scope.

Build phase

PagePurpose
Phase 00 · Sources, tools and test bootstrapPin engine/toolchain/plugin evidence; establish paths, IDs, documentation and dedicated-server build prerequisites.
Phase 01 · Sprite, camera and layering labProve a common body on 3D ground with four facings, zoom, depth, feet and a clothing fallback.
Phase 02 · Three-dimensional locomotionUse CharacterMovement across X/Y with Z height; add jump, sprint, dodge, swim and fall/shoreline rules.
Phase 03 · Dedicated server and two clientsConnect independent clients, possess once, replicate movement and remote appearance intent.
Phase 04 · Accounts and character creationUse a development authenticator boundary; create/list/select a named class/body/appearance record.
Phase 05 · Durable character serviceCreate the versioned schema, command receipts, session fencing and minimal reward/item identities.
Phase 06 · Two-zone handoffAuthor two zone catalogs/gates, allocate two servers and transfer only one player.
Phase 07 · GAS and authoritative combatInitialize PlayerState/enemy ASCs; prove costs, cooldowns, target checks, melee and projectiles.
Phase 08 · AI, defeat credit, XP and recoveryBuild server AI and defeat ledger, minimal party eligibility, XP awards and safe respawn.
Phase 09 · Items, bags and equipmentCreate real inventory UI/stack rules, item requirements and replicated logical/visual equipment.
Phase 10 · Weighted loot and ownershipMaterialize loot once for a defeated spawn generation; expose corpse/container interaction.
Phase 11 · Merchants, currency and bankCommit buy/sell/buyback/repair and deposits/withdrawals through authenticated service commands.
Phase 12 · Randomized mining and woodcuttingSelect eligible sites per zone seed; validate tools, action leases, yield, XP and respawn.
Phase 13 · Crafting professionsLearn recipes, use stations and consume materials/currency atomically for deterministic items.
Phase 14 · FishingValidate shoreline casts, world bobber, bite window, reel and terminal fish reward.
Phase 15 · Village dialogue and quest loopAuthor conditional NPC dialogue and a quest DAG using server gameplay events and receipt-backed rewards.
Phase 16 · Four-class talents and progressionBuild all four ability catalogs, validated skill graph, derived stats and paid respec.
Phase 17 · Exploration and world productionAdd discovery/minimap, time/weather, six region plans and a data-driven content factory.
Phase 18 · Elites, bosses and dungeonsAdd phases/telegraphs, four-player instanced ruin allocation and recovery/loot rules.
Phase 19 · Social and secure tradeExtend minimal parties into invites/chat/friends/block/private messages and escrow trades.
Phase 20 · Reputation, trainers and hubsAdd faction thresholds, profession/class training, safe-hub unlocks and world event participation.
Phase 21 · Guilds and committed growthAdd guild roles/invites, social dashboards, content expansion; mounts stay behind an art/movement gate.
Phase 22 · Operations, security and measured scaleExercise restarts, restores, fencing, dupe attacks, deployment and replication comparisons.
Phase 23 · Packaged release-candidate proofRun complete packaged client/server slices, localization/accessibility and documentation consistency.

System

PagePurpose
Melee sweeps, server projectiles and hit deduplicationSpatial attacks use real 3D collision queries while sprites communicate their timing. The server owns the active window, projectile spawn and effect application, and records which targets have already been attempted for each execution.
Audio, particles and 2D/3D presentation cuesMake accepted actions readable without allowing particles, sprite frames or sounds to grant damage, resources or loot. A missed cue may look wrong but must never leave gameplay stuck.
Bank storage and bag expansionA bank is another owned container under the same item/stack rules, opened through a validated safe service. Moving an item between bag and bank changes location, not identity or total ownership.
Fixed camera, zoom, depth and occluder handlingUse a fixed three-quarter camera that follows the local pawn with clamped zoom. The camera is local presentation: it does not rotate collision, change server movement axes or confer visibility permission for attacks through walls.
Character slots, creation, selection and recoveryCreate a common-body avatar with approved hair/palette/outfit choices and one of Vanguard, Ranger, Arcanist or Warden. Class selection changes authored starting rules, not an invented race silhouette. The backend commits name, slot and appearance together.
Zone/local/party chat, private messages and moderationChat routes authenticated messages to deliberate audiences and enforces limits, blocks and moderation. Local/zone chat is not an unrestricted reliable multicast from any client; private messages and reports require identity-aware routing.
GAS ownership, attributes, costs and predictionUse one Gameplay Ability System stack for health, mana, stamina, abilities, costs, cooldowns and effects. A player's ASC lives on PlayerState during one zone session; the current body is its avatar. An ordinary enemy owns its ASC on its Character.
Consumables, tools and item-use effectsItem use validates an owned consumable/tool and applies its authored effect under one replay-safe operation. Consuming a potion must not grant healing twice on a repeated packet, and a rejected use must not remove the item.
Recipes, professions, stations and deterministic resultsCrafting consumes a validated recipe's resources and produces deterministic output in one durable operation. Blacksmithing, Alchemy, Cooking and Tailoring start as templates with separate profession progression and learned recipe sets.
Death, shrine respawn and reconnect policyDeath replaces the combat body state without wiping progression. A safe shrine/bind point provides recovery; a client reconnect is not allowed to reset inventory, undo a death penalty or refresh all resources for free.
Dedicated-server bootstrap, possession and replicationStart a headless authority process and two independent clients early. GameMode controls admission/spawning in its one server world; PlayerState is an in-zone replicated actor, not a database or a cross-process singleton.
Deployment, zone allocation and operational recoveryOperate a small persistent multi-zone game with measured capacities, reproducible builds, backups and a safe maintenance procedure. A dedicated UE process is a zone simulator, not a complete hosting or matchmaking platform.
NPC roles, branching dialogue and consequence recordsOne NPC may offer dialogue, quests, merchant, trainer and crafting services without duplicating player state. Conditions and choices are authored; lasting consequences are validated character records, not booleans hidden in a widget.
Elite phases, boss telegraphs and instanced dungeonsA small co-op dungeon is an independently allocated zone instance with a declared party roster, encounter state and recovery policy. Boss phases and telegraphs are server decisions; matching does not appear automatically because a dedicated server exists.
Damage, healing, resistances, status effects and interruptionApply combat math and status rules once, through GAS-backed authoritative execution. Healing, damage types, criticals, buffs/debuffs, crowd control and cast interruption are authored rules, not hardcoded UI labels or sprite animation side effects.
NavMesh AI, perception, threat, leash and evadeServer-owned AI moves a capsule over actual 3D walkable surfaces. Use AIController, Behavior Tree, Blackboard, AI Perception and navigation before considering a second decision framework.
Equipment slots, two-hand conflicts and paper-doll visualsEquip valid items into logical stat slots independently of sprite layer coverage. Chest and Top are one slot; Legs and Pants are one slot. A combined outfit sheet cannot be split into independent chest/leg images merely by creating gameplay slots.
Factions, reputation and service unlocksSimple authored factions give recorded standing gains/losses, thresholds and service/quest/price unlocks. Reputation changes come from validated events and should not make required progression permanently impossible.
Safe hubs, roads, boats and paid fast travelLong-distance traversal uses authored roads/gates/boats and later unlocked safe-hub travel. Fast travel is a validated zone-transfer request with optional cost, not a client teleport to an arbitrary map coordinate.
Water casts, bobber, bite, reel and catch transactionFishing is a server-owned timed attempt at an eligible water region. The rod overlay and bobber visualize casting/waiting/bite/reel states; neither a notify nor a delayed packet can create a second catch.
Friends, presence, blocking and account recoveryFriends and block lists are durable identity relationships. Presence is an authorized projection, not a durable promise that a particular actor remains loaded. Account recovery belongs to the authentication provider/service, not an NPC or local save edit.
Mining and woodcutting with exclusive claimsMining and woodcutting share one validated action/claim pipeline but use different tool, animation, profession and yield definitions. Two clients contesting one node cannot both receive its exclusive depleted-generation reward.
Guild membership, roles and durable social administrationGuilds provide durable membership, roles, invitations and guild chat after basic parties/economy operate safely. Initial guilds do not include a guild bank, territory simulation or monetization.
Input, UMG screen ownership, options and accessibilityRoute keyboard/mouse and controller input to one local screen/input owner. UI displays snapshots and sends intents; it cannot pause a shared server, grant items, edit skill ownership or directly mutate replicated attributes.
Interaction targeting, range and modal cleanupOne player-owned interaction component resolves an interactable actor and asks the server to perform a specific action. NPCs, loot, nodes, banks and gates implement a narrow interaction interface without owning the player's inventory.
Inventory bags, stacks, capacity and atomic movesInventory is a bounded collection of stack/instance records. UI drag/drop requests a move; the backend commits ownership and capacity changes. Slot index alone is not a safe identity for a mutable item.
Item definitions, instances, rarities and generated affixesAn authored item definition says what an item can be. An owned gear instance identifies one particular item; a stack row stores a quantity. A world pickup or resource node is a separate source, not the owned item itself.
Capsule locomotion, sprint, jump, dodge and fall damageMove freely on the X/Y ground plane, using Z for elevation. CharacterMovement remains the sole movement integrator. Sprint, jump and dodge consume approved intent/resources; art can have only four directions while collision remains fully three-dimensional.
Accounts, login and environment selectionThe player selects Development or the configured production realm, authenticates, then receives a character list belonging to that verified account. Login establishes identity, not permission to invent inventory or spawn a pawn.
Guaranteed/random loot, corpse access and replay safetyA defeated creature yields a server-created loot allocation with guaranteed entries and weighted rolls. The allocation is generated once per defeat/recipient policy; opening the corpse again never rerolls rarity or produces a second entitlement.
World map, minimap, markers and discoveryA map presents authored geography and server-approved discovery. Minimap position is local presentation of approved movement; hidden quest/resource details are not indiscriminately replicated to every client.
Currency, merchants, stock, buyback and repairsA merchant issues an authoritative quote, then commits currency, inventory, stock and buyback/repair changes together. Store one integer base currency; copper/silver/gold display is a conversion, not three independently editable balances.
Mount feasibility and later movement/content gateMounts are a later committed content system only after movement, camera, collision and animation feasibility pass. No mounted sprite, riding pose, mount creature or equipment compatibility is claimed to exist in the archive.
Replication, interest management and measured scaleSend each client only relevant state while preserving gameplay correctness. Begin with generic Actor replication, then measure before choosing Iris or Replication Graph; do not enable both.
Deferred expansion gates: PvP, raids, housing, auctions and monetizationRecord intentionally deferred ideas so they do not silently become dependencies of the first playable RPG. Each requires a separate approved scope and proof before production systems or UI are exposed.
Parties, invitations, group credit and leadershipA minimal party/eligibility contract is needed before group combat rewards; full invite/leave/leader UI arrives in Phase 19. Party membership is a versioned social record, not a list invented independently by each zone server.
Character persistence, schema, command receipts and sessionsDurability means accepted inventory, currency, quests and progression survive process loss. A UE zone keeps a short-lived authoritative session cache, while one authenticated backend commits durable relational records and audit receipts.
Layered sprites, facing, appearance and remote avatarsRender one 2D body and compatible clothing/weapon layers while a full-height capsule moves on a 3D floor. Presentation selects poses from server-observed action facts; it cannot decide hits, gathering rewards or whether movement is legal.
Levels, derived stats and profession progressionCharacter XP/levels and profession skill are separate durable tracks. The level cap is data-defined; derived combat attributes are rebuilt from class growth, level, equipment, talents and valid effects rather than saved as competing authoritative totals.
Quest DAG, objectives, journal and once-only rewardsQuests track server-approved actions through a versioned dependency graph. The journal is an observer. Gathering, combat, loot, delivery, talk, interaction, exploration, crafting, fishing and dungeon/boss objectives each consume explicit verified events.
Biome resource sites, random placement and respawnChoose resources randomly from intentionally authored eligible sites, not arbitrary map coordinates. Server selection respects biome, surface, navigation, collision, roads, quotas and active/depleted generations, and can be reproduced from recorded zone seed/cycle.
Authentication boundaries, abuse prevention and privacyTreat every network request as untrusted input. Authenticate identity at admission, validate ownership at every command and fence stale server sessions before they can write durable state. Security is a continuing process, not a claim that a dedicated server prevents cheating.
Four classes, talents, prerequisites and respecVanguard, Ranger, Arcanist and Warden share a common body but differ through authored abilities, stat growth and talent graphs. The backend validates points, prerequisites/exclusivity and respec atomically; UI lines on a tree are not rules.
Enemy spawning, defeat ledger, XP and group creditAn encounter owns spawn generations and legitimate participation. Defeat creates a durable receipt before XP/loot success is announced, so corpse reload or server restart cannot reward the same enemy twice.
Water, swimming and shoreline transitionsWater is a 3D volume with a water surface and reachable shoreline, not a sprite animation state. The player can swim without climbing; fishing access and swimming permissions use related water metadata but different action rules.
Soft targets, utility targeting, LOS and telegraphsSoft targeting helps select an enemy or ally, but a selection does not guarantee a hit. Melee/projectile/area rules still use the server's current positions, collision, faction and ability definition.
Diagnostics, economy telemetry and support evidenceMake failures explainable without turning logging into another mutable gameplay database. Economic ledgers provide durable accounting; operational metrics explain latency, rejection and content balance.
End-to-end testing, packaging and release acceptanceProve the integrated player journey in a real packaged client/server environment, while distinguishing documentation static checks from gameplay verification. Release only the measured, tested scope.
Consensual player trading and escrowA secure trade binds both players' acceptances to one immutable offer revision and commits both inventories/currencies together. Never implement trade as one player sending an item followed by a separate payment.
NPC training, recipe unlocks and profession gatesTrainers sell or grant validated ability/profession/recipe unlocks through a service catalog. They do not directly modify skill arrays in a widget or own duplicate progression records.
Content versions, schema migrations and patch compatibilityKeep saved identities stable across renamed assets, new content and software patches. Never interpret an unknown saved item/class/quest as permission to delete player progress.
Biome production, navigation, density and interiorsCreate new authored zones through catalogs, reusable Blueprint actors and content validation instead of changing C++ for every forest or town. Six region designs define a long-term world plan; they are not six finished 3D maps.
World events, ambient villagers and later schedulesSmall server-owned zone events create shared activity without requiring an ecosystem simulator. Ambient villagers/fishers can animate locally; schedules that change service availability require authoritative time and recovery rules.
Shared time, lighting, weather and biome modifiersReplicate a shared server clock epoch and weather state, then let clients render lighting and transitions locally. Fishing/resource modifiers read the authoritative weather/time version, not a client sky material.
Biome servers, loading screens and fenced handoffA player walks through a registered road gate and connects to a different server process while other players remain in the source zone. Internal world streaming can reduce one map's memory use but cannot perform this identity/session handoff.

World design

PagePurpose
Brinewake CoastWater resonators from each region converge at a ruined sea lock. Resolve the regional conflict through a cooperative encounter rather than an endless world simulation.
Kestrel CrownRebuild ridge beacons and decide which faction receives survey records. Either choice retains a route to mountain service access.
MorrowfenFlood gauges disagree with the tide. Craft repaired instruments, fish local species and trace diverted water to the coast.
Rillmere ValleyFirst Steps teaches identity and interaction; Road Supplies repairs a warning post; The Sluice Signal reveals old waterworks being disturbed by survey crews.
ThornwealdThe Wardens investigate hollow resonators that attract predators; the player chooses a recorded diplomatic response, not an irreversible main-story lock.
Varran HallsCompeting guilds seek to restart a pressure engine; expose its failing seals and choose a reversible service alliance.

Planned game assets are not compiled assets. Values are proposals unless explicitly evidenced. Verification and limitations.
